newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady, U.S. market remains supportive.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady, U.S. market remains supportive.

text.p: NWE naphtha was notionally steady on Thursday, with little action seen on the physical market.
Traders said that no cargoes were actively offered but any December cargoes coming on the market were likely to be snapped up quickly by trading houses looking to work vessels transatlantic.
Cargoes were pegged at $224/$225 a tonne cif NWE.
"But anything very prompt would be weaker because there isn't much urgent end-user demand," a dealer said.
Algeria's Skikda oil port remained closed on Thursday due to bad weather, a port official said.
While two major European petrochemical companies had cargoes shut in at Skikda, their prompt requirements appeared to be covered, traders said.
ARA barges were offered at $224 and bid at $221 a tonne.
Dec swaps firmed earlier but slipped back with crude to talk at $223/$224, with Jan around $8/$9 in backwardation.
